title: SpaceX cuts Blackwell chip rental prices by up to 35%; Anthropic-returned H200s subleased at low prices

content_html:
Semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis disclosed two changes this week in a report sent to institutional clients: SpaceX has lowered the rental price for small-scale Nvidia Blackwell GPU clusters, and AI large-model company Anthropic has decided not to renew its lease on a batch of SpaceX H200 chips.

According to the SemiAnalysis report, SpaceX has cut the rental price for small-scale Blackwell clusters from roughly $15 to $15.50 per GPU per hour to $10 to $12, a reduction of between 20% and 35%. The adjusted small-scale rate is now roughly in line with the bulk pricing it offers to major customers such as Anthropic and Google.

This price adjustment reflects the changing supply and demand in the AI computing-power rental market. On one hand, SpaceX is attracting small and mid-sized customers by cutting prices, narrowing the price gap between large and small customers; on the other hand, after Anthropic returns the H200 chips, SpaceX needs to sublease them at low prices to clear its inventory. Taken together, these two changes suggest that demand for renting high-end AI chips may be shifting from a supply shortage toward a rebalancing of supply and demand.
